title: Product protocol runs its factors in parallel
statement:
Let $p_1$ and $p_2$ be private-coin finite-message protocols over the same input types $X$ and $Y$, with output types $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ and private-randomness types $(\Omega_{X_1}, \Omega_{Y_1})$ and $(\Omega_{X_2}, \Omega_{Y_2})$ respectively. Then for all inputs $x : X$ and $y : Y$, and all paired private coins $\omega_x = (\omega_{x,1}, \omega_{x,2}) \in \Omega_{X_1} \times \Omega_{X_2}$ and $\omega_y = (\omega_{y,1}, \omega_{y,2}) \in \Omega_{Y_1} \times \Omega_{Y_2}$, executing the product protocol of $p_1$ and $p_2$ yields the pair
\[
  \bigl(p_1(x, y; \omega_{x,1}, \omega_{y,1}),\; p_2(x, y; \omega_{x,2}, \omega_{y,2})\bigr),
\]
where each component is the output of the corresponding factor run on the same inputs with its own share of the private randomness.
hypotheses_covered: p1 a private-coin finite-message protocol with randomness spaces Ω_X1, Ω_Y1
p2 a private-coin finite-message protocol with randomness spaces Ω_X2, Ω_Y2
both over the same input types X, Y
Alice's coin ω_x in the product space Ω_X1 × Ω_X2
Bob's coin ω_y in the product space Ω_Y1 × Ω_Y2
